findings.title: v1 `arci plan` error output changed for malformed or missing rates
findings.where: src/arci/cli.py:1088-1095 (plan parser: --baseline-rate/--candidate-rate lost type=float and required=True)
findings.claim: The suite plan work made --baseline-rate/--candidate-rate/--target-verdict untyped and optional. The v1 path now converts with float() and checks required options by hand, so v1 invocations print different error text than v1.0.0. That is v1 output changed beyond the fault-accounting section. Only error paths are affected; valid v1 plans are byte-identical. It is blocking by the stated definition, and the caller may downgrade it.
findings.evidence: Same args, main checkout (v1.0.0) vs worktree. `plan --baseline-rate abc --candidate-rate 0.85 --target-verdict PASS`: v1 gives `error: CliError: argument --baseline-rate: invalid float value: 'abc'`, worktree gives `error: ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'abc'`. `plan --baseline-rate 0.9`: v1 gives `error: CliError: the following arguments are required: --candidate-rate, --target-verdict`, worktree gives `error: CliError: the following argument is required: --candidate-rate` (one at a time). Exit codes are equal (3). Normal markdown and json v1 plans compared SAME.
findings.fix: In the v1 branch, parse the rates with the same message argparse used (`argument --baseline-rate: invalid float value: '...'`). Collect every missing required option into one `the following arguments are required: a, b` message in argparse's order. Add a test that compares v1 plan error text with the v1.0.0 strings.

findings.title: Suite plan refuses exact projection for most default grids with a false 'too large' message
findings.claim: Under the default budget, registered_pairs = N*ceil(400/N), which is above 400 for every N that does not divide 400. So 3-, 6-, 7-, 9-cell suites and many others get floors only, with the message 'grid or rational precision too large to enumerate in reasonable time'. The same enumeration takes about 0.1 s, so the printed reason is false and ADR 0011 item 13 projections are unavailable for ordinary suites.
findings.evidence: Default-rule descriptors with 1 condition, homogeneous 0.875/0.75/0.875. N=20 (400 pairs): exact projection in 0.14 s. N=1 (400 rounds): exact in 0.43 s. N=3 (134 rounds, 402 pairs) and N=7 (58 rounds, 406 pairs): status 'grid or rational precision too large to enumerate in reasonable time; floors only'. Calling suite_stats.operating_characteristics directly on those manifests: N=3 in 0.104 s (P(PASS)=4.71e-4, P(BLOCK)=0.170, E[pairs]=379.93); N=7 in 0.047 s. The bits bound is reasonable: a 7-digit rate at 400 pairs took 9.2 s and was refused.
findings.fix: Base the cutoff on actual cost (states x bits, or a measured budget), not a hard 400-pair limit, or raise it to at least the default-budget maximum (N*ceil(400/N) < 800). Say which limit was hit (grid size or rational precision). Add a test with a default 3-cell suite that expects an exact projection.

findings.title: Suite triage drops v1's empty-fixtures limitation
findings.where: src/arci/triage.py:419-428 (_suite_comparison returns TraceCheckResult with default limitations)
findings.claim: v1 check_traces appends 'Fixture identities are empty; environment equality is declaration-only.' when manifest.fixtures_sha256 is empty. The suite adapter rebuilds the comparison from private helpers and never adds it, so suite triage output omits a caveat that v1 shows for the same situation. It still prints 'Integrity seals and declared scenario equality ...', although the suite path performs no _scenario check (pair identity stands in for it).
findings.evidence: The demo suite store (tiny-suite, per_round, 4 rounds) has manifest fixtures_sha256 == ''. `arci triage <suite store>` printed 8 Limitation lines and no 'Fixture identities' line. `arci triage` on each of the four v1 demo stores prints that line once (grep -c = 1 for each).
findings.fix: In _suite_comparison, pass `limitations=_LIMITATIONS + (_EMPTY_FIXTURES,)` when `manifest.fixtures_sha256` is empty, as check_traces does (export the constant or add a small public helper in trace_check). Add a suite triage test that asserts the line. A public trace_check entry point taking two already-loaded trials would also remove the three pyright-ignored private imports.

findings.title: Plan probabilities are shown only as exact rationals hundreds of digits long
findings.where: src/arci/planning.py:247-259 (render_suite_plan) and the projection dict at :198-204
findings.claim: Markdown output prints P(PASS), P(BLOCK), P(INCONCLUSIVE), expected pairs and expected sessions only as exact fractions. Realistic suites produce numerators and denominators of 70 to 350 digits, so a user cannot read the projected verdict probability. The values themselves are correct.
findings.evidence: 200-cell suite, 2 rounds, homogeneous 0.875/0.75/0.875: `PASS: 164611323044906497811042991230574809287...` is a fraction of about 350 digits over 350 digits, and the same holds for every projection line. The 20-cell demo shows about 70-digit fractions. My independent computation shows the values are about 0.038, 0.108 and so on.
findings.fix: Keep the exact string in JSON. In Markdown, add a decimal approximation with directed rounding next to each value, for example ' (about 0.0229%)', never printing exactly 0 or 1 unless the value is exactly 0 or 1.

findings.title: Suite plan markdown cosmetics: tuple repr and a projection disclaimer on floors-only output
findings.claim: The Markdown output prints `stakes: ('1/4', '1/2')` (a Python tuple repr) and `threshold: 40` (gate and triage print 40/1). It also always prints 'These are model projections, not measured live-agent behavior...' even when no model was given and only exact floors are shown.
findings.evidence: `arci plan arci.yaml` (no model) prints the assumptions paragraph with 'These are model projections', then `stakes: ('1/4', '1/2')`, `threshold: 40`, and 'floors only: no model supplied'.
findings.fix: Join stakes with ', '. Use the same threshold spelling as gate. Print the assumptions paragraph only when a projection is present, or say that the floors are exact properties of the rule.

findings.title: `arci plan <v1 manifest.json>` dumps a raw pydantic error
findings.claim: A non-descriptor positional is parsed directly as SuiteManifest. A v1 sealed manifest therefore fails with an opaque multi-error message, not 'plan positional input must be a suite descriptor or manifest', which the code already prints for v1 descriptors.
findings.evidence: `arci plan demo/manifest-agent_a.json --baseline-rate 0.5 --candidate-rate 0.5 --agreement 1` gives `error: ValidationError: 15 validation errors for SuiteManifest ...`, exit 3.
findings.fix: Dispatch on manifest_schema_version first, or catch ValidationError, and print the existing one-line message.

reasoning:
I reproduced this myself. In /Users/ajay/Developer/.arci-worktrees/wt-v2-reports/src/arci/planning.py:192, suite_plan refuses to compute a projection when `manifest.registered_pairs > 400 or bits > 8192`. The default budget is max_rounds = ceil(400/N), from suite_stats.default_max_rounds, so registered_pairs = N*ceil(400/N), and that exceeds 400 whenever N does not divide 400.

I ran the script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/p2breview/cutoff.py with the worktree venv and PYTHONPATH=. It builds suite_manifest(n_tasks=N, n_conditions=1) with default max_rounds and max_errored_pairs, and uses the homogeneous model 0.875/0.75/0.875.
- N=1 (400 pairs): exact projection in 0.36 s.
- N=2 (400 pairs): exact projection in 0.18 s.
- N=20 (400 pairs): exact projection in 0.02 s.
- N=3 (402), N=6 (402), N=7 (406) and N=9 (405): all return the status 'grid or rational precision too large to enumerate in reasonable time; floors only'.

Calling suite_stats.operating_characteristics directly on those same manifests finishes in 0.12 s (N=3), 0.07 s (N=6), 0.06 s (N=7) and 0.05 s (N=9). For N=3 it gives P(PASS)=4.71e-4, P(BLOCK)=0.1702 and E[pairs]=379.93, which matches the finding's numbers. For these laws the bits term is about 4 bits x 402 = 1608, far under 8192, so the pair-count cap alone causes the refusal. That makes the printed reason false.

This contradicts ADR 0011 item 13, which says projections are computed exactly for a stated model. The P2b brief allows refusal only for grids 'too large to enumerate in reasonable time', and these grids are not. This is not blocking: no number, verdict or probability shown to the user is wrong, and the floors are still correct. Fixing it in this phase, rated major, is appropriate.
corrected_claim: planning.py:192 sets a hard cap of registered_pairs > 400. Under the default budget max_rounds = ceil(400/N), that cap refuses the exact suite projection for every grid size N that does not divide 400; I reproduced N=3, 6, 7 and 9. Those grids instead get the false message 'grid or rational precision too large to enumerate in reasonable time; floors only'. The same exact computation (operating_characteristics) actually takes 0.05 to 0.12 s for them, about the same as the accepted N=1, 2 and 20 cases (0.02 to 0.36 s). The fix is to base the cutoff on real cost, or at least to allow the default-budget maximum (N*ceil(400/N) < 800). The message should also name which limit was hit. A test should cover a default 3-cell suite.

corrected_claim: In Markdown, `arci plan <suite>` prints P(PASS), P(BLOCK), P(INCONCLUSIVE), expected_pairs and expected_sessions only as exact fractions (planning.py:198-204 and 247-259), with no decimal. On the 20-cell test manifest each fraction runs to 70-80 digits. reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. Code: in src/arci/trace_check.py, `check_traces` (lines 408-410) adds `_EMPTY_FIXTURES` ("Fixture identities are empty; environment equality is declaration-only.") when `baseline.manifest.fixtures_sha256` is empty. The suite adapter `_suite_comparison` in src/arci/triage.py (about lines 380-428) imports only the private `_first_difference`, `_projection` and `_valid_events`. It builds `TraceCheckResult(...)` without a `limitations` argument, so the result falls back to the class default `_LIMITATIONS`.

Reproduction (my own, run output under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/p2breview/fix1/): I built a suite BLOCK store with the repo's test helpers `store_at` and `add_events` and checked that its manifest has `fixtures_sha256 == ''`. `arci triage <store> --trial <candidate>` exits 1 and gives DRIFT on pair 1. The text output has 8 Limitation lines, 0 'Fixture identities' lines and 1 'Integrity seals' line. The JSON output also has 0 'Fixture identities'.

v1 comparison: `arci demo --keep` produced four v1 stores (agent_a, agent_b, agent_b-noisy, agent_c). `arci triage` on each one prints the 'Fixture identities' line exactly once.

So the suite path drops a caveat that v1 shows for the same empty-fixtures situation. The suite contracts (STATISTICS_SUITE.md, the AGENT_SEMANTICS suite section, 0010, 0011 and the P2b brief) say nothing explicit about this line, so it is a parity and honesty gap, not a breach of a stated contract.

It is not blocking. No number, verdict or exit code is wrong, v1 output is unchanged, and the 'Integrity seals and declared scenario equality do not authenticate...' sentence is a disclaimer, not a claim. Its wording is only slightly off for the suite path, which checks pair identity, not `_scenario`. Major fits: fix it in this phase.
corrected_claim: Suite triage (`triage._suite_comparison`) returns a `TraceCheckResult` with the default `_LIMITATIONS`, so it never adds v1's "Fixture identities are empty; environment equality is declaration-only." line, even when the suite manifest's `fixtures_sha256` is empty. v1 `check_traces` adds that line, and `arci triage` on all four v1 demo stores prints it once. Reproduced on a suite BLOCK store with `fixtures_sha256 == ''`: the text and JSON triage output both have 0 such lines out of 8 Limitations. Fix: when `manifest.fixtures_sha256` is empty, pass `limitations=_LIMITATIONS + (_EMPTY_FIXTURES,)`, preferably through a public trace_check helper, and add a suite triage test that asserts the line.

reasoning:
I reproduced this myself, with run output in the scratchpad's p2breview/plan_err folder. v1.0.0 was run as PYTHONPATH=main/src with the worktree's python and `-m arci plan`. The worktree was run with its .venv/bin/arci.

Three invocations give different stderr between the two versions:
(1) `--baseline-rate abc --candidate-rate 0.85 --target-verdict PASS`: v1 prints `error: CliError: argument --baseline-rate: invalid float value: 'abc'`, the worktree prints `error: ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'abc'`.
(2) `--baseline-rate 0.9`: v1 prints `error: CliError: the following arguments are required: --candidate-rate, --target-verdict`, the worktree prints `error: CliError: the following argument is required: --candidate-rate`.
(3) No arguments: v1 lists all three missing options, the worktree reports only `--baseline-rate`.

Exit codes are 3 in both versions. These cases match between the two versions:
- valid markdown and json plans (stdout identical, rc 0)
- an invalid `--target-verdict` choice
- an out-of-range rate (1.5)

The cause is in src/arci/cli.py:1090-1095. The v1 branch checks required fields one at a time and raises "the following argument is required". It then calls a bare float() on the string value, so the argparse type=float and required=True messages are lost.

The P2b brief, line 6, says "v1 behaviour, output and tests stay byte-identical". The severity rubric also counts any v1 output change beyond the fault-accounting section as blocking. The finding stands as stated. In practice the impact is small: the change is limited to stderr on invalid usage, with the exit code unchanged, and the fix is cheap.
corrected_claim: On the v1 (non-suite) path, `arci plan` prints different stderr text for an unparseable rate and for missing required options. Unparseable rate: `ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'abc'` instead of argparse's `CliError: argument --baseline-rate: invalid float value: 'abc'`. Missing options: one at a time, as `the following argument is required: --X`, instead of argparse's combined `the following arguments are required: a, b, c`. The cause is src/arci/cli.py:1090-1095. Exit codes (3) are unchanged, as are valid-plan stdout, invalid-choice errors and out-of-range errors. The brief requires v1 output to stay byte-identical, so this counts as v1 output changed. The fix is to restore argparse's exact messages on the v1 branch and add a regression test against the v1.0.0 strings.

findings.title: Fault accounting reports a fault from a module:function factory as 'declared, never fired' even when it fired in every trial
findings.where: src/arci/report.py fault_accounting (lines ~36-70); used by v1 render_markdown, suite_report.render_suite_markdown/json and the v1 JSON report
findings.claim: fault_accounting groups injections by the declared FaultSpec.name. But injected_by records Perturbation.name, and for a referenced factory (FaultSpec.name='module:function', allowed by AGENT_SEMANTICS) the two never match. As a result, every injection by a custom perturbation is dropped, and the row shows 0 injections, 0 trials fired and 'declared, never fired'. Those numbers and that status are wrong.
findings.evidence: I wrote a scratch module p2bfault with factory make() that returns a perturbation named 'custom', and ran the demo suite with condition custom_fault declaring FaultSpec(name='p2bfault:make', tool='finish', at_occurrence=0). This was `arci run` into scratchpad/p2breview/runs_custom; it ended PASS at round 8. trials.jsonl contains 160 tool_finish payloads with "injected_by":"custom". `arci report` prints `| custom_fault | p2bfault:make | baseline | 40 | 0 | 0 | declared, never fired |`, and the same row for candidate. perturb.build wraps referenced factories in _ScopedPerturbation(name=perturbation.name), and the inner perturbation sets injected_by=self.name, so the declared name never shows up in events.
findings.fix: Map each declared fault to the name its perturbation actually records. One way is to resolve build(fault).name when accounting, in the same way the runner does. Another is to record the declared FaultSpec.name, or the fault's index, alongside injected_by. Add a test with a module:function factory whose perturbation name differs from the reference.

findings.title: v1 `arci plan` error output changed (missing args, bad float, extra positional)
findings.where: src/arci/cli.py _parser plan_command (--baseline-rate/--candidate-rate now untyped and optional; suite_input positional always present) and _dispatch plan branch
findings.claim: The suite plan rework turned v1's argparse-enforced required and float-typed options into manual checks, and gave the parser a permanent positional argument. Several v1 invocations now print different errors. Exit codes are unchanged (3); only the error text differs. Under this review's rubric, any v1 output change outside the fault-accounting section is blocking.
findings.evidence: I ran the same commands with the v1 main checkout's arci and with the worktree's arci. `plan --baseline-rate 0.9 --candidate-rate 0.9`: v1 prints 'the following arguments are required: --target-verdict', now 'the following argument is required: --target-verdict'. `plan --baseline-rate abc ...`: v1 prints "argument --baseline-rate: invalid float value: 'abc'", now "ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'abc'". `plan --baseline-rate 0.9 --candidate-rate 0.9 --target-verdict PASS extra`: v1 prints 'unrecognized arguments: extra', now "FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'extra'". Normal v1 plan output (md and json) and the other option errors are byte-identical.
findings.fix: Keep v1's exact messages. Emit 'the following arguments are required: ...' with argparse's plural wording and its comma-joined list of every missing option. Validate floats with argparse's 'argument --X: invalid float value' text. Treat a positional that is not a suite input as 'unrecognized arguments: X', or only accept the positional when it is a suite file. Add v1 golden tests for these error paths.

findings.title: Suite `arci report` ignores decision.json: a store whose saved decision mismatches shows a clean PASS with exit 0
findings.claim: The report recomputes decide_suite from the trials and never compares the result with the stored decision.json. It never says whether a stored decision is present. For the same store, `arci gate` reports 'stored decision: MISMATCH (ERROR, exit 3)', while `arci report` shows a clean 'VERDICT: PASS (exit 0)' with no warning. The same happens when decision.json is absent after an interrupted run.
findings.evidence: I copied the demo control store and edited decision.json to verdict BLOCK and exit_code 1 (scratchpad/p2breview/tamper/dec). `arci gate` printed 'stored decision: MISMATCH (ERROR, exit 3)' and exited 3. `arci report` printed 'VERDICT: PASS (exit 0)' and exited 0. With decision.json deleted, gate says 'stored decision: absent' and report again shows plain PASS exit 0. Tampered trial or manifest seals are handled correctly: exit 3 with 'trial seal is invalid' or 'suite manifest seal is invalid'.
findings.fix: Run the same stored-decision comparison as _cmd_suite_gate (replay_suite_decision). Render a 'Stored decision: MATCH / absent / MISMATCH' line in Markdown and a key in JSON. On a mismatch, either return exit 3 or show the mismatch next to the verdict, so that no clean PASS appears for a store the gate rejects.

findings.title: per_round guarantee text loses its context in the report; JSON omits the 'no guarantee averaged over seeds' sentence
findings.claim: The per_round sentence matches STATISTICS_SUITE.md word for word, apart from the dropped bold markers. In the report, though, it starts with a dangling 'Its' (per_round is never named), and it says 'with the independence conditions above' when the report states them in the next paragraph. The JSON report includes only this sentence. It omits 'There is no guarantee averaged over seeds...', which the Markdown report shows. The general ASSUMPTIONS sentence also offers stationarity as an alternative for per_round. Stationarity implies the per-round null, so this is not false, but it is weaker than the document's 'requires'.
findings.evidence: rep_control.md (demo, per_round) shows 'Its error guarantee requires that in every round ... with the independence conditions above ...' directly after the rule block, with the ASSUMPTIONS paragraph below it. `grep -c 'averaged over seeds'` returns 0 for rep_control.json and 1 for rep_control.md. The fixed sentence 'The claim is for the registered scenarios over outcome randomness.' is verbatim.
findings.fix: Prefix the sentence with 'scenario_seeds: per_round.', or quote it as from STATISTICS_SUITE.md. Put the assumptions paragraph before it, or replace 'above' with a reference to it. Add the no-seed-averaging sentence to the JSON 'guarantee' field, or to a separate key.

findings.title: 'Earlier runs on this candidate are never hidden' overclaims for suites
findings.where: src/arci/suite_report.py line 134 (wording inherited from v1 report.py)
findings.claim: Prior-run discovery only looks at the same output root and skips invalid manifests. Sealed-manifest runs never add prior runs. So a report can show this heading with '- None recorded.' even when an earlier run of the same candidate exists.
findings.evidence: I ran man_regression.json a second time into a different --out (scratchpad/p2breview/r7/runs_regression_again). Its report shows '## Earlier runs on this candidate are never hidden' followed by '- None recorded.', while scratchpad/p2breview/runs_regression/offline-suite@f27dc79a... holds the earlier BLOCK run of the same candidate.
findings.fix: Use a heading such as 'Earlier runs recorded in this manifest (prior_runs)'. Add a note that discovery covers only the output root used and that skipped or relocated history is not listed.

findings.title: Suite `arci plan` Markdown prints thousand-digit raw fractions and Python reprs

reasoning:
I reproduced this independently in a fresh run store. I used the sealed manifest scratchpad/p2breview/man_custom.json, in which condition custom_fault declares FaultSpec(name='p2bfault:make', bucket=falsify, tool='finish', at_occurrence=0). The factory p2bfault.make returns a perturbation whose name is 'custom'. I ran it with PYTHONPATH=mod and `arci run man_custom.json --out skeptic_custom`.

What the run recorded: trials.jsonl has 160 events with "injected_by":"custom". There are 80 custom_fault trials in total, 40 per arm, and all 80 contain an injection.

What the report says: `arci report` prints:
- `| custom_fault | p2bfault:make | baseline | 40 | 0 | 0 | declared, never fired |`
- the same row for candidate.

`arci report --format json` returns fault_accounting rows with injections=0, trials_fired=0 and status 'declared, never fired'.

Cause:
- report.fault_accounting builds its keys from the observed injected_by strings, but emits rows only for {fault.name for fault in condition.faults}, so the observed key 'custom' is never looked up.
- perturb.build wraps referenced factories in _ScopedPerturbation(name=perturbation.name), so the factory's own name ('custom') is what gets recorded, never the declared 'module:function' string.
- AGENT_SEMANTICS allows FaultSpec.name to be a module:function factory, and nothing requires the factory's perturbation name to equal that reference.

The result is a wrong count and a wrong status shown to the user. That meets the blocking definition. The function is shared by the v1 and suite markdown and JSON reports.
corrected_claim: The claim holds as stated. For a fault declared as a module:function factory whose perturbation .name differs from the reference string, report.fault_accounting shows 0 injections, 0 trials fired and 'declared, never fired' in both the markdown and JSON reports. I reproduced this with a fresh run in which all 80 custom_fault trials (160 tool_finish events with injected_by='custom') actually fired. The fix is to attribute injections to the declared fault. One way is to resolve build(fault).name when accounting. Another is to record the declared FaultSpec name or index next to injected_by. The fix should come with a regression test that uses a factory whose perturbation name differs from its reference.

reasoning:
Reproduced, working in scratchpad/p2breview/skep. I copied the control store into dec. Untouched, gate exits 0 with 'stored decision: MATCH' and report exits 0 with 'VERDICT: PASS (exit 0)'. I then changed decision.json to verdict BLOCK, exit_code 1. Gate printed 'VERDICT: ERROR (exit 3)', 'recomputed verdict: PASS (exit 0)' and 'stored decision: MISMATCH (ERROR, exit 3)', and exited 3. `arci report` (md) and `arci report --format json` both exited 0. The md output was byte-identical to the untouched report and had no stored-decision line or mismatch note. The code agrees: in cli.py _cmd_report, the suite branch calls load_suite_run, then decide_suite, renders, and returns suite_decision.exit_code. It never reads decision.json. _cmd_suite_gate does compare, using replay_suite_decision.

Narrowed for three reasons. (1) The 'absent' half is not a discrepancy. With decision.json removed, gate also exits 0 with PASS and only adds 'stored decision: absent'. AGENT_SEMANTICS says outright that 'a fully saved decisive round can still be recomputed without a stored decision'. (2) No contract requires the comparison in report. The P2b brief item 1 lists the report contents (verdict and exit code, rule, rounds, wealths, guarantee, cells, prior_runs) and leaves out the stored decision. AGENT_SEMANTICS and ADR 0011 give the stored-decision comparison to `arci gate` only. v1 `arci report` also ignores decision.json and recomputes. (3) The PASS that report shows is not a wrong number. It is the correct recomputation from fully validated, sealed manifest and trials, the same value gate prints as 'recomputed verdict'. Only the unsealed or tampered decision record differs.

What remains is a UX and consistency gap. The suite report returns the decision's exit code (v1 report always returns 0), so it looks like a gate. For a store whose saved decision the gate rejects with exit 3, it still exits 0 and gives no hint. That is worth a 'Stored decision: MATCH/absent/MISMATCH' line later. It is not blocking and not required in this phase.
corrected_claim: For a suite store whose decision.json does not match (edited verdict or invalid seal), `arci report` (md and json) shows the correct recomputed 'VERDICT: PASS (exit 0)', exits 0 and says nothing about the stored decision, while `arci gate` reports MISMATCH and exits 3. The absent-decision case is not a discrepancy, because gate also exits 0 there. The brief and contracts do not require report to compare stored decisions, and v1 report ignores decision.json too. This is a minor consistency improvement (add a stored-decision status line), not a wrong verdict.

findings.title: Custom (module:function) faults are always reported as 'declared, never fired' with 0 injections, even when they fire
findings.where: src/arci/report.py:35-72 (fault_accounting), used by v1 render_markdown, v1 --format json (cli.py:658) and suite_report.py
findings.claim: fault_accounting matches tool_finish.injected_by against FaultSpec.name. For a referenced factory, FaultSpec.name is 'module:function', but perturb.build wraps the factory's Perturbation and injected_by is whatever that perturbation's own `name` is (perturb.py _ScopedPerturbation delegates before/after; toolbox records result.injected_by unchanged). The two never match, so a custom fault that fires in every trial gets Injections 0, Trials fired 0 and the 'declared, never fired' flag. The injections it did record are counted nowhere. The section header's claim that rows are 'grouped by declared fault name' is false for these faults.
findings.evidence: Scratch factory p2bcustom:factory (perturbation name 'slowish', fires on fetch/finish occurrence 0). Real v1 run: good_agent vs budget_swallower, 6 per arm (store synth_v1/exp-acceptance). My raw count from trials.jsonl: 6 tool_finish events with injected_by='slowish' in condition 'custom', baseline arm. Worktree report row: `| `custom` | `p2bcustom:factory` | baseline | 6 | 0 | 0 | declared, never fired |`. Suite run (packaged suite agents, 5 tasks, BLOCK, store synth_suite4/variant): 20 recorded injections in 'custom' (10 per arm). The report shows 0 and 'declared, never fired' for both arms. Paths are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/p2breview/.
findings.fix: Do not compare a 'module:function' declaration by name. Either stamp the declared name into injected_by in _ScopedPerturbation, which changes recorded traces and needs an explicit decision, or attribute it on the report side. Report-side rule: for each condition and arm, injected_by values that match no registered declared name go to the referenced declaration when there is exactly one; otherwise show them in an 'unattributed' row. Never print 'declared, never fired' for a referenced factory while unattributed injections exist in that arm. Add tests with a working custom factory in v1 and in a suite.

findings.title: A same-name duplicate declaration that never fires is reported as 'observed'
findings.where: src/arci/report.py:70 (rows keyed by sorted set of fault.name)
findings.claim: Rows come from the set of fault names. Two declarations with the same name but different tool or occurrence collapse into one row. If one fires and the other never does, the row reads 'observed', so the brief's requirement to flag a declared fault that never fired is not met. The report text discloses that same-name declarations are indistinguishable, but they can usually be told apart: tool_finish records tool and call_id, the matching tool_start records the occurrence, and FaultSpec has tool and at_occurrence.
findings.evidence: v1 run synth_v1, condition 'dup' = tool_timeout on fetch@0 plus tool_timeout on store@5; the agent never reaches store occurrence 5. Report row: `| `dup` | `tool_timeout` | baseline | 6 | 6 | 6 | observed |`, a single row. The store@5 declaration never fired and is not flagged. Suite variant: condition 'dup' with tool_timeout on finish@0 and finish@5 gives the same single 'observed' row for both arms.
findings.fix: Key each row by the declaration (index, name, tool, at_occurrence). Attribute each injected tool_finish to the declaration whose tool and occurrence match, taking the occurrence from the tool_start with the same call_id. For decision_unavailable, the match is occurrence >= at_occurrence. Where attribution is ambiguous, say so in the row ('cannot attribute') rather than 'observed'.
